_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::beams#7 — CROSSAREA, MOMIN2, MOMIN3 and MOMINPOL of MAT_BeamReissnerElastHyper are four independent inputs and 4C never checks that they describe the same section. Two arms on one cantilever loaded axially and transversely: a genuine r=0.1 circle, and the same second moments with CROSSAREA 1.0 (the 'A = 1.0 but Iyy = 0.01 for a circular section' mistake the entry names). Both parse, both converge, both finish all ten steps, and CROSS_SECTION_WARNINGS=0 — the code says nothing. The consequence is asymmetric and that is the part worth knowing: the axial response follows A and flips sign, while the bending response is untouched to under one per cent, so a bending-only sanity check will not catch it. The numbers are read back out of 4C's own result-test lines, forced to print by an unmatchable RESULT DESCRIPTION. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf).

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: give the second arm the consistent circular area too. The two arms then agree exactly, so the axial sign flip disappears and the fixture must go red.
